report.summary: Chunk 4 of 5: completes build_index by computing clone clusters, building resolver, scoring hotspots, adding optional layers (naming, documents, wiki, types), and returning the index dict. Defines _RESOLVER_CACHE, _scope_key, resolution_context, and _build_lock.

handoff.purpose: Complete build_index function and define cache/lock utilities

symbols.name: _RESOLVER_CACHE
symbols.note: Module-level dict caching SymbolResolver instances keyed by scope_key.

symbols.name: _scope_key
symbols.note: Returns a string key combining root, scope fingerprint, and optional layer flags (docs, types, wiki).

symbols.name: resolution_context
symbols.note: Retrieves a cached SymbolResolver by key or by resolved repo root path.

symbols.name: _INDEX_CACHE
symbols.note: Module-level dict caching index dicts keyed by scope_key.

symbols.name: _BUILD_LOCKS
symbols.note: Module-level dict mapping scope_key to threading.Lock for serializing index builds.

symbols.name: _build_lock
symbols.note: Returns a threading.Lock for a given key, creating one if absent.

claims.text: unit_clusters computes the exact fingerprint, renamed_clusters computed it again plus the abstract one, and near_clusters derived the abstract one a third time.
claims.why: The functions unit_clusters, renamed_clusters, near_clusters are called but not defined in this chunk; their behavior is not visible.

claims.text: Normalization and abstraction are the two most expensive operations in the scan.
claims.why: No performance data or profiling is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Memo = CloneMemo(spec_by_lang) is scoped to this call and dropped with it -- a module-level cache would leak across scans.
claims.why: The variable memo is local to the build_index function and not stored in any module-level cache visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Stash the derived symbol resolver so consumers (slice.py) can sharpen call edges without rebuilding; CodeUnits are not JSON-serializable so it lives in a side cache, never in the returned (serializable) index dict.
claims.why: _RESOLVER_CACHE is a module-level dict that stores the resolver separately from the index dict; the index dict is returned without resolver.

claims.text: Keyed by root + SCOPE, exactly like ``_INDEX_CACHE``.
claims.why: Both _RESOLVER_CACHE and _INDEX_CACHE are keyed by the same scope_key string (produced by _scope_key).

claims.text: Keying it by root alone made the two caches disagree: an unscoped build of the same root overwrote the scoped resolver, and a later scoped slice hit _INDEX_CACHE (so no rebuild repaired it) and resolved callees against a defs_by_file that still contained SHELL units -- pulling a vendored body into a slice the center was supposed to exclude.
claims.why: This describes a historical bug; the current code uses scope_key which includes scope, so this scenario is prevented. The claim is about past behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: DOCUMENT SECTIONS ARE IN THE RESOLVER, AND ONLY THERE. ``build_resolver`` uses units for one thing -- ``defs_by_file`` -- and ``resolve`` consults that map only for the querying file itself and for files it IMPORTS. Nothing imports a document (document links are kept out of ``import_targets_by_rel`` on purpose), so a heading can never be returned as the resolution of a code identifier.
claims.why: The build_resolver function and resolve method are not defined in this chunk; the claim about their behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: What it CAN do is the thing the defect needs: ``context_plan._symbol_names`` reads ``defs_by_file`` wholesale to build the BM25 lexical corpus, so heading titles become searchable evidence and a specification stops being invisible to the planner.
claims.why: context_plan and its _symbol_names method are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Documents stay OUT of ``all_units`` so no clone pass sees prose.
claims.why: The construction of all_units is not shown in this chunk; the claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: AND NOTHING TYPE-SHAPED IS IN THAT ARGUMENT LIST (invariant I2). The type layer resolves annotations against its OWN ``typegraph.types_by_file`` table, which is never merged in here.
claims.why: The argument list to build_resolver is shown to include all_units and doc_units, but the type layer's involvement is not visible.

claims.text: If a class were in ``defs_by_file`` it would displace a same-named function (``resolve`` takes the first match), and if a field name were, ``graph.callees`` -- which resolves EVERY identifier token in a body -- would turn ``path``, ``root``, ``name``, ``line``, ``source`` into fabricated CALL edges in every slice.
claims.why: The behavior of resolve and graph.callees is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: HOTSPOTS ARE A CODE-HEALTH RANKING, so documents are not in it. Left in, a 1,800-line handoff scores loc/50 = 36 -- competitive with real rot, with no code in it at all -- and ``spine/picker.hotspot_candidates`` turns a hotspot row into a work item reading 'extract the long functions, keep every public name and signature'. Against a document that instruction is self-contradictory and nothing downstream rejects it.
claims.why: The claim about hotspot scoring and downstream behavior is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: ADDITIVE AND GATED. An unconfigured repo with nothing to report must produce a byte-identical index to before this change, so the key is present only when there is something to say.
claims.why: The code shows extra['python_naming'] is set only if scope.center or naming_report['ambiguous_count'] is truthy, otherwise extra remains empty; the returned dict includes extra only when non-empty.

claims.text: SAME GATE, SAME REASON as ``python_naming``: present only when there is something to say. With documents off the returned dict has no document keys at all, so a pre-document consumer sees the dict it always saw.
claims.why: The document-related keys are added to extra only if docs_on is True; otherwise extra remains empty and the returned dict has no document keys.

claims.text: With documents ON, the block is never silent about what it withheld -- an unresolved link is a relation the map is NOT showing, and an unreported one is indistinguishable from a document that links to nothing.
claims.why: The code includes n_links_unresolved in the extra['documents'] dict, explicitly reporting unresolved links.

claims.text: The document relation layer, kept SEPARATE from ``import_edges``. A link is not an import: it carries no name binding, it does not make the target a dependency, and folding it in would silently move ``fan_in``, ``fenced_dominance`` and every reachability answer derived from the import graph.
claims.why: The code stores document links in extra['document_links'] and extra['document_links_reverse'], separate from import_edges which is a top-level key. They are never merged.

claims.text: OWN LAYER, never merged into document_links. A doc->doc wikilink and a doc->code reference are different relations, and `type_refs` are names NOBODY resolved -- publishing them as edges would assert a binding that was never made.
claims.why: The code stores wiki links in separate keys: wiki_links, wiki_code_links, wiki_type_refs, wiki_embeds, distinct from document_links.

claims.text: SAME GATE, SAME REASON as ``documents``: three keys that are simply absent when the layer is off, so a pre-type consumer sees the dict it always saw.
claims.why: The code updates extra with type_blocks only if types_on is True; otherwise extra remains unchanged.

claims.text: ``type_nodes`` and ``type_edges`` are a SEPARATE NODE NAMESPACE (``type:rel#Qual`` / ``field:rel#Qual.name``) and a SEPARATE RELATION LAYER, for the reason a document link is not an import, one level sharper: a type node has no bytes on disk at all.
claims.why: The contents of type_blocks are not shown in this chunk; the claim about node namespaces cannot be verified.

claims.text: Folding either into ``modules`` or ``import_edges`` would put a node with no forward edges into ``graph._graph_nodes`` -- diluting ``fenced_dominance``'s denominator, so the fence's stand-down threshold stops firing and every task stays on the premium lane.
claims.why: The graph module and its behavior are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: NEVER let exclusion be silent -- a shrunken duplication report that does not say what it dropped reads exactly like a clean bill of health (the same trap as report.truncated / S6's max_files ceiling).
claims.why: The ignored dict in the returned index includes count, n_files_scanned, scope description, sample, and truncated flag, making exclusions explicit.

claims.text: Documents obey the same scope, so a shell document is a withheld file exactly like a shell source file and is counted as one. With documents off both addends are zero and the numbers are unchanged.
claims.why: The handling of doc_ignored and doc_records is not fully visible; the claim about scope behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: Bounded sample, sorted for determinism -- the full list can be tens of thousands of paths on a vendored tree.
claims.why: The sample is computed as sorted(ignored | doc_ignored)[:25], which is sorted and truncated to 25 entries.

claims.text: Same edges, but keyed rel->rel for EVERY language. ``dependencies`` mixes namespaces (dotted module names for Python, rel paths for the rest), so it cannot be joined against ``modules``/``hotspots``. The code map needs one consistent node id, and this is it.
claims.why: The content of import_targets_by_rel is not shown; the claim about namespaces cannot be verified.

claims.text: Additive; the slicer needs caller identities and ``fan_in`` only carries COUNTS.
claims.why: The index includes import_edges_reverse which provides caller identities in addition to fan_in counts.

claims.text: Tie-break on the module name. ``fan_in`` is populated by iterating dep_edges' SETS, so its insertion order varies with PYTHONHASHSEED; since sorted() is stable, equal-count entries used to come out in a different order on every process. Same counts, now a total order.
claims.why: fan_in is sorted by (-kv[1], kv[0]), which uses module name as secondary key, ensuring deterministic ordering.

claims.text: Type-3 does not cover every language it parsed. Saying so is not optional: a caller who sees C files scanned and zero near-clusters would otherwise read 'no near-duplication in C' when the truth is 'C was never asked'.
claims.why: The duplication dict includes near_excluded_languages key listing languages excluded from Type-3 clustering, making the exclusion explicit.

claims.text: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for both ``_INDEX_CACHE`` and ``_RESOLVER_CACHE``. They are two views of one build and MUST agree; when they were keyed by different expressions they drifted apart and a scoped index was served with an unscoped resolver.
claims.why: Both caches are keyed by the same _scope_key function, ensuring consistency.

claims.text: An unscoped repo keeps its bare path key, so nothing changes for repos that never configure this.
claims.why: When unscoped is True (no center and no ignore), base is set to str(resolved) (bare path).

claims.text: ``documents`` is part of the key for the same reason ``scope`` is: a document-bearing index is a DIFFERENT index (different ``modules``, different ``total_tokens``, an extra relation layer, and a resolver whose ``defs_by_file`` carries heading titles).
claims.why: If documents is True, base is extended with '+docs', making the key distinct.

claims.text: ``types`` is part of the key for exactly that reason and no weaker one: a type-bearing index carries three keys the other does not, so serving one for the other presents as the layer silently missing in one process and silently present in the next.
claims.why: If types is True, base is extended with '+types', making the key distinct.

claims.text: THE SUFFIX ORDER IS FIXED -- ``base`` then ``+docs`` then ``+types`` -- so the four flag combinations produce four distinct keys and no two of them can collide by being spelled in a different order.
claims.why: The code appends '+docs' before '+types', and '+wiki' after, in that fixed order.

claims.text: Lets ``slice.py`` reuse Move-4 resolution without recomputing the whole index.
claims.why: slice.py is not in this chunk; the claim about its usage cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``key`` is an index's ``scope_key``; pass it whenever you hold the index dict, so a SCOPED index gets the resolver built under that same scope rather than whichever build last touched the bare root.
claims.why: The function uses the provided key to lookup in _RESOLVER_CACHE; if key is None, it falls back to bare root lookup.

claims.text: Omitting it keeps the historical bare-root lookup for unscoped callers.
claims.why: If key is None, the function uses str(Path(repo_root).resolve()) as the cache key, which is the bare root path.

observations.what: The build_index function is very long and contains extensive inline documentation explaining design decisions and invariants.
The _RESOLVER_CACHE and _INDEX_CACHE are both keyed by the same _scope_key function, ensuring consistency.
The resolution_context function provides a fallback to bare root lookup when key is None, maintaining backward compatibility.
The _build_lock function is defined but not used within this chunk; it is likely used elsewhere for thread-safe index building.
